public records relating to an agenda item on this agenda are available for the public inspection at the time the records

2.  Wastewater Treatment Plant Lab and Casino Showers and Restrooms Roof Remediation
  and Replacement
  The City is addressing multiple critical roofing deficiencies across key public facilities,
  including the Wastewater Treatment Plant Laboratory located on Pebbly Beach Road
  and the Casino Showers and Restrooms located along St. Catherine Way.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or their designee to develop and solicit a request for
  proposals (RFP) from qualified contractors for replacement of the Wastewater
  Treatment Plant (WVVTP) Lab Roof (including sloped roof addition), and remediation
  and replacement of the Casino Showers and Restrooms Roof.

GENERAL BUSINESS

3.  Authorize Procurement of LUCAS Device, Stryker Power Gurney & Power Chair with
  Measure B Funding
  The Avalon Fire Department (AFD) requested Measure B funding for Emergency Medical
  Services (EMS) equipment including a powered ambulance gurney, powered stair chair,
  and LUCAS 3 Chest Compression System. These tools will directly enhance our EMS
  service.
  Recommended Action
  1. Authorize City Manager to procure, per the City’s purchasing policy, a LUCAS 3 Chest
  Compression System, Stryker Power Gurney and Stryker Power Chair, that meets the
  required specification outlined by staff, for a total not to exceed $102,730.06 (10245-
  6547) 2. Exempt this procurement from competitive bidding and make the affirmative
  finding that Stryker is a sole source vendor of these devices.

4.  Approval of Rebuild for Public Works Telehandler
  The Public Works Department relies on a 2005 Caterpillar TH58OB telehandler to support
  essential daily operations, including material handling, infrastructure maintenance, and
  logistical functions throughout the city. The unit is over 20 years old and requires a
  comprehensive rebuild to maintain operational reliability and safety.
  Recommended Action
  1. Authorize the City Manager or their designee to execute all necessary agreement to
  complete a certified rebuild of the City’s 2005 Caterpillar TH58OB telehandler by Quinn
  CAT in an amount not to exceed $70,000, and approve an additional appropriation of up
  to $20,000 for rental equipment and barge transportation costs incurred during the rebuild
  period. 2. Make the affirmative finding Quinn CAT is the only provider in Southern
  California offering a Caterpillar-certified rebuild program, meeting the requirements for
  the sole-source procurement policy outlined in Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.111(b).
  3. Amend the 2025-2026 Capital Budget Account 13825-6781 to include $90,000 for
  —

  the refurbishment of the telehandler.

5.  Resolution Approving and Adopting Public Participation Outreach and Disruption of
  Remote Access Policies
  SB 707 amended the Brown Act to require eligible legislative bodies to take certain
  actions to encourage residents, including those in underrepresented communities and
  non-English-speaking communities, to participate in public meetings. To comply with SB
  707, the City Attorney’s Office drafted two policies for City Council consideration.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution approving and adopting Public Participation Outreach and Disruption
  of Remote Access Policies in compliance with SB 707.

ADJOURN

on Friday, May 1, 2026 on the City’s website, www.cityofavalon.gov/agendacenter, and at City
Hall, 410 Avalon Canyon Road.

Devin Elise Hart, Senior Management Analyst

SUBJECT:  Wastewater Treatment Plant Lab and Casino Showers and
  Restrooms Roof Remediation and Replacement

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager or their designee to develop
and solicit a request for proposals (RFP) from qualified contractors for:
  1. Replacement of the Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) Lab Roof (including
  sloped roof addition), and
  2. Remediation and Replacement of the Casino Showers and Restrooms Roof.

REPORT SUMMARY:  The City is currently addressing multiple critical roofing
deficiencies across key public facilities, including the Wastewater Treatment Plant
(WWTP) Laboratory located on Pebbly Beach Road and the Casino Showers and
Restrooms located along St. Catherine Way.

Wastewater Treatment Plant Lab Roof
The Wastewater Treatment Plant Lab roof has significantly deteriorated and continues to
experience recurring leaks despite multiple temporary repair efforts. The existing flat roof
system has reached the end of its useful life and poses an ongoing risk to laboratory
equipment, electrical systems, and the integrity of the building structure.

Given the age and condition of the roof, and the critical function of the laboratory in
supporting regulatory compliance and plant operations, staff recommends proceeding
with the solicitation of proposals from qualified contractors to perform a full roof
replacement. The proposed project includes installation of a new sloped roof system over
the existing flat roof, which will serve as a long-term solution with an expected service life
of approximately 20—30 years. The new system will improve drainage, reduce
maintenance, and provide redundancy by maintaining the existing roof as a secondary
barrier. The scope of work includes:
  • Removal of existing roofing materials.
  • Installation of new roof framing and sheathing.
  • Upgraded waterproof membrane and flashing systems.
  • Ventilation improvements and a sloped roof system to improve long-term drainage.
  • Electrical and finish work.

Based on a recent Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate, the total project cost
for the WVVTP roof replacement is approximately $145,000, including materials, labor,
 shipping, contingency, and contractor overhead and general conditions. This project is
included in the City’s Capital Improvement Program.

Casino Showers and Restrooms Roof
The Casino Showers and Restrooms roof is in poor condition with broken, cracked, and
missing tiles; deteriorated asphalt roofing materials; exposed and deteriorating plywood
sheathing; and failing fascia boards and flashing systems. Immediate remediation and
replacement is recommended to prevent further deterioration and water intrusion. The
scope of work includes:
  • Full removal and replacement of roofing materials.
  • Replacement of damaged sheathing and fascia boards.
  • Installation of new waterproofing membrane, asphalt shingles, and composite tiles.
  • Replacement of deteriorated windowsill and flashing components.

Based on a recent Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate, the total project cost
is approximately $125,000, including labor, materials, shipping, contingency, and
contractor overhead and general conditions.

Staff proposes to release separate or combined Requests for Proposals (RFPs) to solicit
bids from experienced license qualified contractors to complete these projects. These
improvements are necessary to:
  Protect critical infrastructure and public facilities.
  • Maintain regulatory compliance at the WWTP.
  • Ensure safe and functional public amenities along the waterfront.
  • Reduce long-term maintenance and emergency repair costs.

The informal bid procurement process will be utilized in accordance with Avalon Municipal
Code Section 3-4.205. The proposed timeline for the REP is as follows:

as a future agenda item following receipt and evaluation of proposals.

SUBJECT:  Authorize Procurement of LUCAS Device, Stryker Power Gurney &

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Authorize City Manager to procure, per the City’s purchasing
policy, a LUCAS 3 Chest Compression System, Stryker Power Gurney and Stryker Power Chair,
that meets the required specification outlined by staff, for a total not to exceed $102,730.06
(10245-6547) 2. Exempt this procurement from competitive bidding and make the affirmative
finding that Stryker is a sole source vendor of these devices.

REPORT SUMMARY: In June 2025, the City requested Measure B funding from Los Angeles
County Emergency Medical Services Agency thought the Measure B Advisory Board. The City
was notified in January 2026 that the request had been awarded for the full amount, with a
contract being executed in March 2026.

The Avalon Fire Department (AFD) requested Measure B funding for Emergency Medical
Services (EMS) equipment including a powered ambulance gurney, powered stair chair, and
LUCAS 3 Chest Compression System. These tools will directly enhance our EMS service,
ensuring comprehensive medical care for our community and over one million visitors to Catalina
Island annually. Automated Chest Compression Devices help during life threatening cardiac
arrests, power gurneys reduce firefighter injury risk and improve patient transport safety, and
stair chairs improve the efficiency of facilitating the movement of patients up/down stairs in hilly
neighborhoods and uneven city surfaces.

The LUCAS Device addresses both limitations. It takes over the role of one person scene.
Allowing that potential initial smaller crew to administer other critical lifesaving skills. It also
provides a pre-established rate, rhythm, and quality of CPR that does not decline overtime. This
continued, highly accurate CPR is the cornerstone of resuscitation and cardiac arrest
survivability. Power gurneys and stair chairs provide enhanced patient care and comfort,
allowing for a smoother, more controlled transfer of patients, and a reduction in the risk of falls
and discomfort. They also meet dynamic crash test standards for increased safety during
transport. Power gurneys and stair chairs also significantly reduce the spinal load on firefighters,
preventing cumulative trauma injuries associated with repetitive lifting and lowering of
patients. Power gurneys provide support during loading and unloading, further minimizing the
risk of patient drops and injuries. Although power gurneys may have a higher initial cost, the
reduction in injuries can lead to cost savings in the long run through reduced workers’

REPORT SUMMARY: Senate Bill 707 (SB 707) amended the Brown Act to require eligible
legislative bodies to take certain actions to encourage residents, including those in
underrepresented communities and non-English-speaking communities, to participate in public
meetings and adopt procedures for interruptions of meetings.

To comply with SB 707, the City Attorney’s Office drafted two policies for City Council
consideration and approval.

Public Participation and Outreach Policy
This Policy establishes the reasonable efforts the City of Avalon will take to invite groups that do
not traditionally participate in public meetings to attend its meetings under the Brown Act
(Government Code § 54953.4(b)(3)(C)). This Policy is intended to support inclusive public
engagement while preserving the City’s discretion to determine and adjust appropriate outreach
methods based on local needs, priorities, and available resources.

Within 9 months of the adoption of this Policy, City Staff will prepare and present to the City
Council a list of organizations, media outlets, and other entities that may assist in expanding
awareness of the City Council’s meetings. This list may include, but is not limited to,
  • Media organizations that provide news coverage, including media organizations that
  serve non-English-speaking communities; and
  • Community-based organizations such as good government groups, civil rights
  organizations, civic engagement organizations, neighborhood associations, and other
  community or cultural groups active in the City’s jurisdiction, including organizations
  active in non-English-speaking communities.

The list may be updated periodically as determined appropriate by the City Council or designated
staff.

 The City Council may periodically review its outreach practices and make adjustments as
appropriate. In doing so, it may consider factors such as community feedback, participation
levels, resource availability, and evolving communication practices.

In addition to the outreach efforts described in this Policy, the Brown Act establishes additional
public access requirements intended to support broad participation in public meetings of eligible
legislative bodies like the City Council. These requirements include, among other things:
provisions related to the translation of meeting agendas into applicable languages (if applicable),
the availability of a public meetings webpage with specified information in required languages (if
applicable), systems for requesting agendas and meeting materials, and accommodations that
facilitate public participation, including assistance for interpretation.

The policy may be amended by the City Council at their discretion.

Disruption of Telephonic or Internet Service During Meetings
This policy establishes procedures for responding to a disruption in the telephonic or internet
services that provide two-way remote public access to meetings of the City Council of the City
of Avalon, as required by the Brown Act (Government Code section 54953.4). The policy ensures
transparency, public participation, and the continuation of meetings during technological
disruptions.

This policy applies to all open and public meetings of the City Council at which remote public
participation is required under the Brown Act.

When remote public access is required under the Brown Act, the City Council shall provide
members of the public with an opportunity to attend and participate in the meeting using a two-
way audiovisual platform or a two-way telephonic service, provided that adequate telephonic or
internet service is operational at the meeting location.

Members of the public participating remotely shall be provided the same opportunity to provide
public comment as members of the public attending in person, including the same time allotment.

The policy also addresses what actions must be taken in response to a service disruption, and
the response to members of the public that may cause a disturbance to a meeting.

This policy may be amended by the City Council at their discretion.

  4. Outreach Methods

Using the above list, the City Council may provide direction to staff to utilize a variety of
outreach methods, depending on available resources and community needs. These may
include direct distribution of meeting information through e-mail or other notification
systems; posting of meeting information on the City of Avalon’s website or other digital
 platforms; use of social media or electronic communications; and coordination with media
outlets or community organizations to share information about upcoming meetings.

The City Council may also provide direction to staff to consider partnerships with
community-based organizations or other stakeholders to help disseminate information to
broader or underrepresented audiences. Where feasible, outreach efforts may include
the use of multilingual communications, culturally relevant messaging, or engagement
through media outlets serving diverse communities.

Nothing in this Policy, however, requires the use of any particular outreach method.

  5. Role of Staff

The City Council may assign responsibility for supporting outreach efforts to appropriate
City of Avalon staff, including but not limited to the City Clerk’s office, Communications
staff, or other designated personnel. Staff responsibilities may include maintaining or
updating outreach contact lists, preparing and distributing outreach materials,
coordinating with community organizations or media outlets, and recommending outreach
strategies for consideration by the City of Avalon. Staff may also assist in identifying
opportunities to improve outreach based on experience, feedback, or changes in
community needs.

  6. Documentation and Reporting

The City Council may request periodic summaries of outreach efforts for informational
purposes. Such summaries may include general descriptions of outreach activities
undertaken, categories of organizations or groups contacted, and observations regarding
participation or engagement trends. Reporting may be provided on a periodic basis as
determined by the City Council and is not intended to require detailed tracking of every
outreach activity.

  7. Evaluation and Adjustment

The City Council may periodically review its outreach practices and make adjustments as
appropriate. In doing so, it may consider factors such as community feedback,
participation levels, resource availability, and evolving communication practices.

  8. Discretion and Limitation

This Policy is intended to provide general guidance and does not create mandatory duties
or obligations. The City Council retains broad discretion in determining what constitutes
reasonable outreach efforts. Consistent with applicable law, failure to provide outreach or
notice to any specific organization or group shall not give rise to any claim or liability.

  9. Additional Brown Act Public Access Requirements

In addition to the outreach efforts described in this Policy, the Brown Act establishes
additional public access requirements intended to support broad participation in public
 meetings of eligible legislative bodies like the City Council. These requirements include,
among other things: provisions related to the translation of meeting agendas into
applicable languages (if applicable), the availability of a public meetings webpage with
specified information in required languages (if applicable), systems for requesting
agendas and meeting materials, and accommodations that facilitate public participation,
including assistance for interpretation.

  10. Review and Updates

This Policy may be amended by the City Council at a public meeting in open session.
   City of Avalon Policy:
  Disruption of Telephonic or Internet Service During Meetings

  1. Background

Senate Bill 707 (2025) amended the Brown Act to require eligible legislative bodies to
adopt, on or before July 1, 2026, a policy addressing how the agency will respond to
disruptions in telephonic or internet service that prevent members of the public from
participating remotely.

  2. Purpose
This policy establishes procedures for responding to a disruption in the telephonic or
internet services that provide two-way remote public access to meetings of the City
Council of the City of Avalon, as required by the Brown Act (Government Code section
54953.4). The policy ensures transparency, public participation, and the continuation of
meetings during technological disruptions.

  3. Definitions
“Service Disruption” means any failure, outage, or other interruption to the agency’s
remote access services that prevents members of the public from participating in a City
Council meeting through the remote access service.

“Disrupting” means engaging in behavior during a meeting of the City Council that
actually disrupts, disturbs, impedes, or renders infeasible the orderly conduct of the
meeting and includes, but is not limited to one of the following:

  a. A failure to comply with reasonable and lawful regulations adopted by the City
  Council of the City of Avalon.

  b. Engaging in behavior that constitutes use of force or a true threat of force.

“Remote access services” means the two-way telephonic service and/or two-way
audiovisual platform used to provide real-time remote public attendance and
observation of meetings.

“Two-way audiovisual platform” means an online platform that provides participants with
the ability to participate in a meeting via both an interactive video conference and a two-
way telephonic service.

“Two-way telephonic service” means a telephone service that does not require internet
access and allows participants to dial a telephone number to listen and verbally
participate.

“True threat of force” means a threat that has sufficient indicia of intent and seriousness,
that a reasonable observer would perceive it to be an actual threat to use force by the
person making the threat.

   4. Applicability

This policy applies to all open and public meetings of the City Council at which remote
public participation is required under the Brown Act. Consistent with the Brown Act, this
policy shall not apply to the following meetings:

  a. Meetings held to attend a judicial or administrative proceeding to which the City
  of Avalon is a party.

  b. Meetings held to inspect real or personal property provided that the topic of the
  meeting is limited to items directly related to the real or personal property.

  c. Meetings held to meet with elected or appointed officials of the United States or
  the State of California, solely to discuss a legislative or regulatory issue affecting
  the City of Avalon and over which the federal or state officials have jurisdiction.

  d. Meetings held to meet in or nearby a facility owned by the City of Avalon,
  provided that the topic of the meeting is limited to items directly related to the
  facility.

  e. Meetings held in an emergency situation pursuant to Government Code section
  54956.5.

  5. Remote Public Access Generally

When remote public access is required under the Brown Act, the City Council shall
provide members of the public with an opportunity to attend and participate in the
meeting using a two-way audiovisual platform or a two-way telephonic service, provided
that adequate telephonic or internet service is operational at the meeting location.

If adequate telephonic or internet service is not operational at the meeting location, the
City Council shall not be required to provide remote access. If adequate telephonic or
internet service is operational for only a portion of the meeting, the City Council shall
provide remote access during that portion of the meeting.

If a two-way audiovisual platform is used, the City Council shall:

  a. Publicly post and provide a call-in option as well; and
  b. Activate any automatic captioning function that is available in the audiovisual
  platform.

If a two-way audiovisual platform is not provided, the City Council shall provide a two
way telephonic service.

Members of the public participating remotely shall be provided the same opportunity to
provide public comment as members of the public attending in person, including the
same time allotment.

   6. Response to Service Disruption

If the City Manager, Mayor or City Clerk becomes aware of a service disruption;

  a. The City Manager, Mayor or City Clerk shall immediately announce the service
  disruption to the public.

  b. The Mayor shall call for a recess of the open session and may convene the
  legislative body in an authorized closed session, consistent with the Brown Act.
  The recess shall last for one hour or until service is restored, whichever is earlier.

  c. During the recess, City of Avalon staff shall make a good faith effort to diagnose
  and restore the disrupted service.

  7. Reconvening the Open Session

After the expiration of the hour, if service has not been restored, the City Manager,
Mayor or City Clerk shall report on the status of staff’s efforts to restore remote access
services, and the City Council may reconvene to:

  a. Adjourn the meeting;

  b. Extend the recess to allow staff more time to make a good faith effort to restore
  remote access services; or

  c. Continue the open session portion of the meeting by adopting, by roll call vote,
  the following or a substantially similar finding:

“The City of Avalon has made good faith efforts to restore telephonic or internet service
in accordance with its adopted policy, and the public interest in continuing the meeting
outweighs the public interest in remote public access.”

Upon adoption of the finding, the City Council may continue the open session portion of
the meeting despite the fact that remote access services have not been restored.

  8. Recordkeeping

The City Clerk shall enter a brief statement into the meeting minutes, including:

  The nature and time of the service disruption;

  The time the meeting was reconvened (if applicable);

  e  Any finding adopted pursuant to Section 7.

  9. Response to Members of the Public Disrupting a Meeting

If the City Manager, Mayor or City Clerk becomes aware of a member of the public who
is attending the meeting through remote access services and is disrupting the meeting

 or otherwise preventing other members of the public from attending or observing the
meeting remotely or in-person:

  a. The Mayor shall warn the person who is participating through remote access
  services that he or she is disrupting the meeting and his or her failure to cease
  that behavior may result in his or her removal.

  b. If the person to whom the Mayor gave the above warning persists in disrupting
  the meeting, the Mayor shall order staff to:

  i.  mute or otherwise limit the individual’s ability to disrupt the meeting, while
  allowing the individual to continue to observe and attend the meeting; or

  ii.  remove the individual from the meeting if paragraph (a) does not address
  the disrupting behavior or is not available using the remote access
  service.
